title: LinkedIn 把 search 棧改成 LLM-centric——重寫的不是 ranker，是「query 怎麼被理解」這層
summary: LinkedIn 工程團隊把整個 search stack 改成 LLM-centric——query understanding 換成 1.5–4B 微調 LLM 取代 NER + 啟發式拼盤、retrieval 用 dual-tower bi-encoder + GPU exhaustive kNN 對 1.6B+ 文件（NDCG@10 0.838）、ranking 用 7B → 1.7B → 0.6B 三段蒸餾出的 SLM cross-encoder（NDCG@10 0.9239）。L4 efficiency 三道壓縮（pruning、RL summary、embedding compression）把 throughput 從 290 推到 22,000 items/sec/GPU（76×），對 teacher NDCG 只跌 2.6%。Evaluation 走 LLM-as-judge calibrated 到 weighted Cohen's Kappa ≥ 0.8，把 release cycle 從週縮到時。Online click AUC 從 0.61 升到 0.67。
widget_questions: Which layer in the four-layer LinkedIn search stack (query understanding LLM, dual-tower EBR, SLM cross-encoder ranker, serving efficiency) owns which responsibility, and what does each NOT do?

What is the shape of the throughput-vs-quality tradeoff curve as the SLM goes through three compression stages (raw 0.6B distilled → pruning → RL summary → embedding compression), and why does LinkedIn pick the rightmost point at 22,000 items/s/GPU and NDCG@10 0.9239 despite the teacher reaching 0.9484?

How does prompt token budget for the query understanding LLM trade latency (quadratic in self-attention) against quality (S-curve saturating around the middle), and where is the production sweet spot inside the 2048-token hard cap?

How does dragging across four compression checkpoints (raw 0.6B, +pruning, +RL summary, +embedding compression) move the (throughput, NDCG@10) point, and which checkpoint corresponds to an actual production-viable working point?
What does the dual-tower bi-encoder do that a single-tower cross-encoder cannot, given the constraint of running exhaustive kNN on a GPU-resident index of 1.6B+ document embeddings?
